content: Anthranilic acid is an organic compound with the chemical formula C6H4(NH2)CO2H. In its pure form, it appears as a white solid, although commercially available samples may exhibit a yellowish hue. The molecular structure of anthranilic acid consists of a benzene ring with two adjacent functional groups: a carboxylic acid (-CO2H) and an amine (-NH2). Due to the polar nature of these functional groups, anthranilic acid is highly soluble in water. It is sometimes referred to as vitamin L. Anthranilic acid is biosynthesized from chorismic acid. It serves as a precursor to the amino acid tryptophan, which is formed through the attachment of a ribose molecule to the amine group of anthranilic acid. Anthranilic acid has a variety of applications. It is used as an intermediate in the production of dyes, pigments, and saccharin. Additionally, anthranilic acid and its esters are utilized in the preparation of perfumes, pharmaceuticals, and UV-absorbing agents. It also functions as a corrosion inhibitor for metals and as a mold inhibitor in soy sauce. Furthermore, anthranilic acid is employed in organic synthesis to generate the benzyne intermediate, a reactive species used in various chemical reactions.
